meta.title: Landing (EN)
meta.footerStory: From the Greek stēlē — the standing stone an inscription is carved into, and stone. Inscribed to last.

properties.title: The CMS your editors can't break.
properties.lede: Every record is a file in your repo, every publish is a git commit, the output is static — and the support phone stays quiet.

properties.title: Three calls that never come
properties.sub: The support calls that arrive after handoff, and the mechanism that makes each one impossible.

calls.body: It can't be. Editors write JSON records through /admin; the site itself is static HTML built from them. There is no template to edit and no database to corrupt.
It can't be. Internal links are picked from a list of real pages and verified at build time. A broken link fails the build instead of reaching production.
You can. Every publish is a commit, so yesterday's text is a revision in git — restoring it is a menu item, not an archaeology project.

properties.title: Deploy on a Friday.
properties.sub: Six guardrails, each a mechanism rather than a policy.

rails.title: Draft branch
rails.body: Save is not publish. Drafts commit to a separate branch and never touch the live build.

rails.title: Page-by-page publish
rails.body: Publishing is per page. One editor finishing the about page can't push another's half-written pricing copy.

rails.title: Link verification at build
rails.body: Internal links are chosen from a list and checked when the site builds. A broken one stops the build.

rails.title: Automatic 301
rails.body: A moved page keeps its old address: the redirect is written for you when the slug changes.

rails.title: Conflict protection
rails.body: Two editors can't overwrite each other — a stale edit is rejected instead of silently winning.

rails.title: Scheduled publish
rails.body: Set a date and the commit lands then. Nobody stays up to press a button.

properties.title: Every publish is a commit.
properties.body1: A record is a JSON file in your own repository. The admin writes it, git stores it, Astro builds it into static HTML. Undo is a menu item because history is git history.
properties.body2: Git-based like Decap and Keystatic — the difference: Stelstone knows your site's routes.

properties.title: From empty account to live in about ten minutes
properties.sub: One Cloudflare Worker runs site, admin and API together. No KV, no extra config.
properties.loopBody: Install, open /admin, watch the commit land. That's the whole loop.

properties.body: The deliverable is a word-by-word mechanical verification report: every page, every paragraph, checked against the original.
